audits.title: Audit of section 2 and section 3 mental health act paperwork in Derby inpatient psychiatric units using an audit tool by Mason et al. (2012)
audits.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 criteria, using the Mason et al. (2012) audit tool
audits.setting: Inpatient psychiatric units, Derby (Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Mental disorder and nature or degree well documented; why informal admission was inappropriate reasonable; poor compliance for justification of risk to health, safety or others, lowest for health (figures not reported).

audits.other_findings: Results presented at local teaching; inclusion in junior doctor induction recommended.
audits.citation: Pearson A, Horton A, Akroyd M. Audit of section 2 and section 3 mental health act paperwork in Derby inpatient psychiatric units using an audit tool by Mason et al. (2012). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S98-S98.

audits.title: Quality Improvement Project to Improve the Implementation of Mental Health Act Code of Practice Guiding Principles and Patient Knowledge About MHA in In-Patient Psychiatric Unit
audits.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice guiding principles
audits.setting: In-patient psychiatric unit, Delfryn House, Cygnet Health Care

cycle1.result: Initial audit of MHA documentation, patients' legal rights, section 17 leave, capacity and treatment forms, tribunal reports, section 117 meetings and managers' hearings identified gaps (figures not reported).

audits.intervention: Weekly email template for MHA actions, section paper scrutiny template, MHA actions added to morning handover and review form, easy-language leaflets, pharmacist and nurse discussion slots, nurse teaching on report writing and tribunals.

cycle2.result: 100% in capacity assessments, treatment certificates and timely reports; patient knowledge of rights and MHA improved by 68% on pre/post score.

audits.other_findings: Organising managers' hearings before section renewal still needed improvement.
audits.citation: Tahseen H, Parry N. Quality Improvement Project to Improve the Implementation of Mental Health Act Code of Practice Guiding Principles and Patient Knowledge About MHA in In-Patient Psychiatric Unit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S113-S113.

audits.title: Quality Improvement Project Investigating the Quality of Completed Section 5(2) Forms
audits.standard: Proforma of 12 criteria for correct completion of Section 5(2) forms
audits.setting: Large acute NHS hospital, adult and paediatric medicine

cycle1.result: 84% of criteria met (202/240); 100% legally valid; 70% identified risks; 55% correct status deletions; 55% contained abbreviations; 40% stated detention was needed to allow MHA assessment.

audits.other_findings: Hospital revising Section 5(2) guidance and preparing example templates; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Cornish E. Quality Improvement Project Investigating the Quality of Completed Section 5(2) Forms. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S126-S126. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10355.

audits.title: Optimizing Mental Health Act Referrals: A Quality Improvement Project to Enhance Documentation and Ensure Least Restrictive Practice in an Acute Hospital Setting
audits.standard: MHA Code of Practice; target at least 95% completion of core assessment and capacity-to-consent documentation within six months
audits.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, Chesterfield Royal Hospital (acute hospital)

cycle1.result: 33% (10/30) of MHA referrals did not result in detention; 90% of patients without a recorded core assessment and 70% without documented capacity were admitted informally or discharged.

audits.intervention: Two PDSA cycles being implemented: mandatory digital fields in the referral pathway (core assessment, capacity, consideration of informal admission) and structured teaching for MHLT staff with visual prompts.
audits.other_findings: Follow-up audit planned; baseline compliance percentage for documentation not given.
audits.citation: Williams O, Azam B. Optimizing Mental Health Act Referrals: A Quality Improvement Project to Enhance Documentation and Ensure Least Restrictive Practice in an Acute Hospital Setting. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S353-S353. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11754.

audits.title: Implementation of an Evidence Based Guideline for Assessment and Documentation of the Civil Commitment Process.
audits.standard: American Psychiatric Association recommended 11 domains of assessment
audits.setting: Two crisis intervention centres in a rural area of a south-eastern US state; six civil commitment examiners

cycle1.result: 25.5% of evaluations contained all 11 APA domains.

audits.intervention: Evidence-based documentation form for civil commitment evaluations plus one-to-one education session for each examiner
audits.other_findings: Commitment rates rose among family practice-trained examiners (60% to 77.3%) and fell among psychiatric-trained examiners (83.75% to 77.66%).
audits.citation: Perrigo TL, Williams KA. Implementation of an Evidence Based Guideline for Assessment and Documentation of the Civil Commitment Process. Community Ment Health J. 2016;52(8):1033-1036. doi:10.1007/s10597-014-9816-6. PMID: 25535054.

audits.title: The integration of mental health care act in primary care: an audit of the use of mental health care act forms for patients´ admission and the effect of continuing medical education on health professionals´ performance of usage, based on Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital´s experience, in Maun, Botswana.
audits.standard: Mental health care act requirement for required admission forms
audits.setting: Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital, Maun (district hospital)

cycle1.result: Required admission MHCA forms used in nil cases.

audits.intervention: Continuing medical education session on MHCA forms
audits.other_findings: At three months use was 64.6% (n=51/79), with no difference between 3 and 6 months; 36/235 (15.3%) forms not used with required companion forms.
audits.citation: Mbuka DO, Tshitenge S, Ogunjumo AJ. The integration of mental health care act in primary care: an audit of the use of mental health care act forms for patients´ admission and the effect of continuing medical education on health professionals´ performance of usage, based on Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital´s experience, in Maun, Botswana. Pan Afr Med J. 2021;40:49. doi:10.11604/pamj.2021.40.49.26114. PMID: 34795829.
